paragraphs.title: Baasha Fortifies Ramah and Asa Turns to Aram

easy.explanation: Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and built Ramah.
easy.q: Who came up against Judah and built Ramah?

answers: People going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah
easy.explanation: Baasha built Ramah to let none go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.
easy.q: What did Baasha intend to prevent by building Ramah?

easy.explanation: Asa sent silver and gold to Ben-hadad king of Syria.
easy.q: To whom did Asa send silver and gold?

answers: So that he would build Ramah
So that he would break his league with Baasha and attack Israel
So that he would bury Asa in the city of David
medium.explanation: Asa asked Ben-hadad to break his league with Baasha and make Baasha depart from him.
medium.q: Why did Asa turn to Ben-hadad?

answers: To prevent movement into or out of the area
medium.explanation: The phrase describes blocking travel and movement through Judah.
medium.q: What does the phrase “let none go out or come in” mean in this passage?

answers: He sent the captains of his armies to attack cities in Israel
medium.explanation: Ben-hadad sent his army captains against the cities of Israel and smote cities in the north.
medium.q: What did Ben-hadad do after listening to Asa?

answers: Baasha's building of Ramah caused Asa to seek help from Syria
Asa's burial caused Ben-hadad to attack
The building of Geba caused Baasha to come against Judah
challenge.explanation: Baasha threatened Judah's roads by building Ramah, so Asa appealed to Ben-hadad.
challenge.q: What cause-and-effect relationship is described in these verses?

answers: Asa mentioned a league between himself and Ben-hadad and between their fathers
Asa mentioned his burial in the city of David
challenge.explanation: Asa said, “There is a league between me and thee, as there was between my father and thy father.”
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Asa's proposed league was based on an earlier relationship between the kings?

answers: Jerusalem and the city of David
challenge.explanation: Ben-hadad's army smote Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim, and the store cities of Naphtali.
challenge.q: Which cities are named among those smitten by the Syrian army?

paragraphs.title: The Building of Ramah Stops and Judah Fortifies Geba and Mizpah

easy.explanation: Baasha left off building Ramah and let his work cease.
easy.q: What did Baasha do when he heard about the Syrian attack?

easy.explanation: Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the building materials.
easy.q: Who carried away the stones and timber of Ramah?

easy.explanation: Asa used the stones and timber of Ramah to build Geba and Mizpah.
easy.q: Which places did Asa build with the materials from Ramah?

answers: To deal with the Syrian attack
medium.explanation: Baasha stopped the work after hearing about Ben-hadad's attack on the cities of Israel.
medium.q: Why did Baasha stop building Ramah?

answers: He used them to build Geba and Mizpah
medium.explanation: The stones and timber from Ramah were used to fortify other places in Judah.
medium.q: What did Asa do with the building materials left at Ramah?

medium.explanation: The expression refers to cities used as storage or supply centers.
medium.q: What were the “store cities of Naphtali” mentioned in the preceding verses?

answers: They were first intended for Ramah and later used for Geba and Mizpah
They were first intended for burial and later for war
They were first intended for Damascus and later for Naphtali
challenge.explanation: The materials Baasha had used at Ramah were transferred for construction elsewhere in Judah.
challenge.q: What change in the purpose of the building materials took place in these verses?

answers: The work was a public action of the kingdom of Judah
Only the people of Ramah took part
The work was done by the king of Syria
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that Asa involved all Judah in the task.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that all Judah helped carry the materials?

answers: Asa built Ramah, Ben-hadad stopped the work, and Baasha built Geba
Ben-hadad attacked, Baasha stopped building Ramah, and Asa used its materials
Baasha built Mizpah, Asa imprisoned Ben-hadad, and Judah burned Ramah
challenge.explanation: The Syrian attack caused Baasha to stop, after which Asa used the materials from Ramah.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is correct?

paragraphs.title: Hanani Rebukes Asa for Relying on Aram

easy.explanation: Hanani the seer came to Asa and rebuked him.
easy.q: Who came to Asa and rebuked him?

easy.explanation: Hanani said that Asa had relied on the king of Syria and not on the LORD.
easy.q: On whom had Asa relied instead of relying on the LORD?

answers: He placed him over the army
He put him in a prison house
easy.explanation: Asa was angry with Hanani and put him in a prison house.
easy.q: What did Asa do to Hanani after the rebuke?

answers: The victory over the Ethiopians and the Lubims
The victory over the people of Ramah
medium.explanation: Hanani reminded Asa that the LORD had delivered the Ethiopians and Lubims into his hand.
medium.q: Which victory did Hanani mention to show that Asa had already received help from the LORD?

answers: Because Asa relied on the LORD alone
Because Asa relied on the king of Syria
medium.explanation: Hanani said that Asa's reliance on Syria caused the Syrian army to escape from him.
medium.q: According to Hanani, why had the host of the king of Syria escaped from Asa?

medium.explanation: Hanani declared that Asa had acted foolishly by relying on Syria.
medium.q: What does “thou hast done foolishly” mean in Hanani's rebuke?

answers: The LORD seeks to strengthen those whose heart is perfect toward him
The LORD helps only those who appeal to the king of Syria
The LORD does not see what people do
challenge.explanation: Hanani said that the eyes of the LORD run throughout the earth to show himself strong for those devoted to him.
challenge.q: What principle does Hanani present about the LORD's relationship with people?

answers: From that time Asa would have wars
Asa would have no more enemies
challenge.explanation: Hanani told Asa, “from henceforth thou shalt have wars.”
challenge.q: What future consequence did Hanani announce because of Asa's actions?

answers: He oppressed some of the people
He sent messengers to the Ethiopians
challenge.explanation: The passage says that Asa oppressed some of the people at the same time.
challenge.q: What did Asa do in addition to imprisoning Hanani?

easy.explanation: Asa was diseased in his feet in the thirty and ninth year of his reign.
easy.q: In which year of his reign was Asa diseased in his feet?

easy.explanation: Asa died in the one and fortieth year of his reign.
easy.q: In which year of his reign did Asa die?

easy.explanation: Asa was buried in his own sepulchres in the city of David.

answers: He sought not the LORD, but the physicians
He asked Ben-hadad to heal him
medium.explanation: The text says that in his disease Asa sought not the LORD, but the physicians.
medium.q: What does the passage say about Asa's response during his illness?

answers: Sweet odours, spices, and a very great burning
The rebuilding of Ramah and a military procession
A payment of silver to Syria
medium.explanation: His burial included a bed filled with sweet odours and spices and a very great burning.
medium.q: What did Asa's burial ceremony include?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the time when Asa was suffering from his disease.
medium.q: What does “in his disease” mean in this passage?

answers: Both passages emphasize that Asa did not properly rely on the LORD
Both passages describe victory over the Ethiopians
Both passages describe the building of Ramah
challenge.explanation: Hanani condemned Asa's reliance on Syria, and the later account says Asa did not seek the LORD during his illness.
challenge.q: What thematic connection exists between Hanani's rebuke and the account of Asa's illness?

answers: His disease became very great, and afterward he died
He recovered immediately and ruled for many more years
He died before he was diseased in his feet
challenge.explanation: The passage describes a severe disease in Asa's feet and then his death in the forty-first year.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the sequence of Asa's illness and death?

answers: He was buried without any ceremony
A perfumed bed was prepared and a very great burning was made
He was buried at Ramah, which Baasha had built
challenge.explanation: His burial included sweet odours, spices, and a very great ceremonial burning.
challenge.q: Which detail distinguishes Asa's burial from a simple burial?
